stopped_because: ran the 5 iterations it was given
policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The cube slides back and forth along a line that passes through the target; every time it crosses the target line counts as one arrival at the target. The goal instruction names the ordinal N (second, third, fifth...). The button must be pressed one arrival early: when N-1 arrivals have happened and the predicted Nth arrival is at most 30 timesteps away, so the press, which takes roughly 25-30 timesteps to land, lands as the cube reaches the target for the Nth time. An episode starts in A: at the first step (empty memory, gripper raised out of the frame and not yet above the button) choose A 'move to the top of the button to prepare'. No point is needed. At every later step (gripper is already positioned above the button, fingers closed), first update memory as instructed (crossings, scene_frame, first_cross_t; the crossing that brings crossings to N-1 often happens inside the frames of the very step where the decision is made), then decide using the updated crossings and first_cross_t values alone: - Predict the timing. The cube starts at rest at one extreme of its swing at t=0, so first_cross_t is a quarter period and the Nth arrival at the target is predicted at T_N = (2N-1)*first_cross_t. Compute remaining = T_N - (timestep of the scene at this decision step). While first_cross_t is empty, crossings is 0 and no timing is needed. - Do not read the cube's direction or speed from the frames to make the decision: cube speed varies threefold across episodes and changes around the turnaround, and the predicted arrival time computed from first_cross_t decides on its own. - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if and only if crossings == N-1 AND remaining <= 30 timesteps (the press takes roughly 25-30 timesteps to land, so it is started once the predicted Nth arrival is at most 30 timesteps away). Whether the cube is still running out, stopped at its turnaround, or already heading back toward the target makes no difference: being past the turnaround or moving back is not enough while remaining > 30. No point is needed. - Otherwise choose B 'remain static'. This covers: crossings < N-1 (even if the cube is heading toward the target, let it pass), and crossings == N-1 while remaining > 30, whatever the cube is doing (the step right after the (N-1)th crossing, however slowly the cube is gliding; the cube on its way out to the far end; the cube stopped at the turnaround; and the cube already past the turnaround and heading back toward the target, as long as more than 30 timesteps remain). If crossings somehow exceeds N-1, or the situation matches no rule above, choose C immediately. Never choose A after the first step.

fields.name: crossings
fields.description: Take the crossings count carried in (0 at the first step, since memory is empty). Build the sequence: the side of the carried-in scene_frame (smaller_x if its cube_x < its target_x, else larger_x; skip if memory is empty), then the side (cube_x < target_x -> smaller_x, cube_x > target_x -> larger_x) of each frame shown at this step in time order, ending with the scene at this step. Add 1 for every consecutive pair in that sequence whose side differs. Write the result. e.g. 2

fields.name: first_cross_t
fields.description: Carry it unchanged if it is already set. If it is empty and the crossings count you just computed at this step is 1 or more, find the first consecutive pair in this step's side sequence whose side differs; the earlier member is either the carried-in scene_frame or a frame of this step, the later member is a frame of this step. With t1, t2 their timesteps, d1 = cube_x - target_x at the earlier frame (its own target_x) and d2 likewise at the later frame, write t1 + (t2 - t1) * |d1| / (|d1| + |d2|), rounded half up to a whole timestep. Never extrapolate; the carried-in scene_frame always supplies the frame before a flip that precedes this step's first frame. Otherwise leave it empty. e.g. 30

fields.name: scene_frame
fields.description: Write the ordered list [timestep, cube_x, target_x] of the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown). Overwrite it every step; at the first step it is the t=0 frame. The side of the target line for any frame is smaller_x if cube_x < target_x, else larger_x; the carried-in scene_frame gives the side, timestep and positions of the last frame of the previous step, and is the frame before the flip whenever a crossing lies between the previous scene and this step's first frame. e.g. [56, 104, 117]
